items.title: TikTok updates its AI video ad tools | Social Media Today
items.summary:
TikTok has added some new elements to its artificial intelligence-powered Symphony ad creation tools, including advanced video generation using the latest models, an updated Symphony API and broader access to AI usage tokens.

First, TikTok added more capacity to generate video ads using the latest Dreamina Seedance AI models within its Symphony Agent tool.

TikTok Symphony update [...] TikTok said advertisers will now be able to upload up to 50 multimodal references (images, videos, and audio), up from 9 previously, while the updated Seedance models will now be able to generate up to 30 seconds of video for each prompt, up from a previous 15-second maximum.

TikTok said the latest Dreamina Seedance model is also able to generate sharper, more realistic imagery and offer better lighting and character consistency across video frames. [...] The company also expanded access to its BytePlus tokens, which will enable more use of its Symphony tools for visual generation.

“Starting November 9, advertisers outside North America can purchase BytePlus tokens to access Dreamina Seedance AI models through Symphony, enabling faster video generation, higher-quality output, and more formats,” TikTok said.

BytePlus is the enterprise technology arm of TikTok parent company ByteDance, and it manages all of the company’s AI tools and systems.

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary:
At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm (bất định) của hàm \(x^2\) là:

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đó \(C\) là hằng số tích phân (cần thêm vì việc lấy đạo hàm của hằng số cho kết quả bằng 0).

items.title: TikTok updates its AI video ad tools | Social Media Today
items.summary:
TikTok has added some new elements to its artificial intelligence-powered Symphony ad creation tools, including advanced video generation using the latest models, an updated Symphony API and broader access to AI usage tokens.

First, TikTok added more capacity to generate video ads using the latest Dreamina Seedance AI models within its Symphony Agent tool.

TikTok Symphony update [...] TikTok said advertisers will now be able to upload up to 50 multimodal references (images, videos, and audio), up from 9 previously, while the updated Seedance models will now be able to generate up to 30 seconds of video for each prompt, up from a previous 15-second maximum.

TikTok said the latest Dreamina Seedance model is also able to generate sharper, more realistic imagery and offer better lighting and character consistency across video frames. [...] The company also expanded access to its BytePlus tokens, which will enable more use of its Symphony tools for visual generation.

“Starting November 9, advertisers outside North America can purchase BytePlus tokens to access Dreamina Seedance AI models through Symphony, enabling faster video generation, higher-quality output, and more formats,” TikTok said.

BytePlus is the enterprise technology arm of TikTok parent company ByteDance, and it manages all of the company’s AI tools and systems.

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary:
At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. [...] protect residents, and ensure that the benefits of AI infrastructure are broadly shared. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said.
